The read record is not passed to the password-change call: the two hashes are inputs, not proven products of the offline read.

Python module-level code only imports ctypes and defines update_race; all native loads and calls are inside that uncalled function. C++ and Rust likewise define routines without a caller. Rust receives the leaked file handle from the harness; C++ and Python open it through CreateFileTransactedW.

No obfuscated payload or archive members. Ordinary Windows path escaping and Rust UTF-16 conversion represent native strings. Facts have no parser errors; flow producer records may-flow/reachability and Python nested-helper/Rust field limitations.

BENIGN is favored by exact-hash provenance as intentionally generated detection fixtures and their partial harness-only packaging, not by clean scans or merely by failure to execute. Embedded exploit operations remain accurately detected. There is no supplied deployment history or harness; use within an unauthorized exploitation chain would change the contextual assessment.
